lines: Because this wall has risen out of the Thames more than 220 times.
The river is tidal. A storm surge from the North Sea can push water straight into the city.
So in 1982, London put 10 steel gates across 520 meters of river.
The biggest weigh 3,300 tonnes and stand as tall as a five-story building.
Most days they lie flat on the riverbed, and ships sail right over them.
They guard 125 square kilometers of the city. That's why London doesn't flood.
